{
"Testing": "The systematic process of evaluating software to verify that it behaves as expected and meets specified requirements, ensuring correctness and quality.",
"Software Correctness": "The property of software that indicates it behaves according to its specification and produces the expected outputs for given inputs.",
"Software Quality": "A measure of how well software meets functional, performance, reliability, and maintainability standards, often validated through testing practices.",
"Unit Test": "A test that verifies the behavior of an individual component or function in isolation from the rest of the system.",
"Integration Test": "A test that verifies multiple components or modules work correctly together as a combined unit.",
"End-to-End Test": "A test that validates complete user workflows by exercising the entire application stack from start to finish.",
"Component": "A discrete, modular unit of software, such as a function, class, or module, that performs a specific role within a larger system.",
"User Workflow": "A sequence of actions and interactions a user performs to accomplish a goal within a software application.",
"Mock": "A test double that simulates the behavior of a real dependency, allowing verification of interactions during unit testing.",
"Stub": "A test double that provides predefined, canned responses to calls made during testing, standing in for real components.",
"Dependency": "An external component, service, or module that a piece of software relies on to function correctly.",
"Canned Response": "A predefined, fixed output returned by a stub or mock in place of a real computation or external call during testing.",
"Test-Driven Development": "A software development methodology in which tests are written before the implementation code, driving design through iterative test-code-refactor cycles.",
"Implementation": "The actual source code that realizes the intended functionality of a software component or system.",
"Code Coverage": "A metric that quantifies the proportion of source code executed by a given test suite, indicating how thoroughly code is tested.",
"Test": "A procedure or piece of code designed to verify that software behaves as expected under specific conditions."
}
